rows.stem: The correct balanced chemical equation showing exothermic reaction in which natural gas burns in air is :
rows.solution:
Methane burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water, releasing heat. Balancing: one C on each side gives one \(\mathrm{CO_2}\); four H give two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\); then four O atoms are needed on the right, so two \(\mathrm{O_2}\):

\(\mathrm{CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O}\) + Energy

The choice must be balanced and show the energy released, which is option (D).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: The warning sign shown in the given figure must invariably be displayed/pasted on the containers which contain hydroxide of :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the hazard symbol (a red-bordered triangular warning sign: liquid dripping from two test tubes onto a surface and onto a hand) is printed only as a picture; the stem never names it, and naming it would give the answer. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
The sign is the warning for a corrosive substance. Sodium hydroxide is a strong, corrosive alkali, so its containers must carry it. The hydroxides of calcium, magnesium and aluminium are much weaker or only slightly soluble.

This is option (C) Sodium.

rows.stem: The body of human beings works within the pH range of :
rows.solution: The human body works within the narrow pH range of about 7.0 to 7.8. This is option (C) \(7{\cdot}0\) to \(7{\cdot}8\).

rows.stem: Aluminium powder is used in thermit welding because :

options.label: A
options.text: Its reaction with iron is highly exothermic.

options.label: B
options.text: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained.

options.label: C
options.text: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten aluminium oxide is obtained to join railway tracks.

options.label: D
options.text: Its melting point is low as compared to iron and a molten alloy of iron and aluminium is formed on heating which is used to join railway tracks.

rows.solution:
In the thermit reaction aluminium reduces iron(III) oxide, and so much heat is released that the iron produced is molten:

\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_2O_3(s)}\) + heat

The molten iron is used to join railway tracks. This is option (B) When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained.

rows.stem: Two metals zinc and tin are dissolved separately in definite proportions in molten copper (the primary metal) to obtain two different alloys respectively known as :
rows.solution: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc; bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. With zinc and tin taken in that order, the alloys are brass and bronze, which is option (C) Brass and Bronze.

rows.stem: The opening and closing of stomata is regulated by :

options.label: D
options.text: Amount of water in guard cells

rows.solution: The guard cells swell when water flows into them, opening the stomatal pore, and shrink when they lose water, closing it. This is option (D) Amount of water in guard cells.

rows.stem: One-cell thick blood vessels are known as :
rows.solution:
The smallest blood vessels, with walls only one cell thick, are the capillaries. Exchange of materials between blood and the cells happens across them.

This is option (B) Capillaries.

rows.stem: Observe the given figures A and B. When *chhui-mui* (sensitive) plant is touched, its leaves fold. This is due to :

options.label: C
options.text: Change in amount of water in cells

rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs, Figure A (a chhui-mui leaf spread open) and Figure B (the same leaf folded); the stem already states that the leaves fold when touched. Page idx 6.
rows.solution: When the leaves of the sensitive plant are touched, the cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them, which makes the leaves fold. This is option (C) Change in amount of water in cells.

rows.stem: *Bryophyllum* produces new plant through :

options.label: A
options.text: Apical buds formed on the tip of the plant

options.label: B
options.text: Vegetative buds produced in the notches of the leaf

options.label: C
options.text: Flowers produced in the notches of the branches

options.label: D
options.text: Fruits formed on the branches of the plant

rows.solution: Bryophyllum produces buds in the notches along the margin of its leaves; when these fall on soil they grow into new plants. This is option (B) Vegetative buds produced in the notches of the leaf.

rows.stem: The number of chromosomes in a cell division is halved. This kind of cell division is observed in :
rows.solution:
Halving the chromosome number happens in meiosis, which forms the gametes. Gametes are made in both the testis (sperms) and the ovary (eggs).

This is option (C) Ovary and testis both.

rows.stem: If the absolute refractive indices of two media X and Y are \(\dfrac{6}{5}\) and \(\dfrac{4}{3}\) respectively, then the refractive index of Y with respect to X will be :
rows.solution:
The refractive index of Y with respect to X is \(n_{YX} = \dfrac{n_Y}{n_X} = \dfrac{4/3}{6/5} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{10}{9}\).

This is option (A) \(\dfrac{10}{9}\).

rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. If its real and inverted image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror, the focal length of the mirror is :
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror with a real image, both distances are on the object side: \(u = -30\) cm, \(v = -60\) cm.

\(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{3}{60}\), so \(f = -20\) cm.

This is option (B) \(-20\) cm.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: In the given figure the angle of incidence and the angle of deviation respectively are :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a ray passing through a triangular glass prism with dashed normals and dashed ray extensions; the seven angles the options name (1 to 7) are numbered only on the drawing. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The angle of incidence is the angle between the incident ray and the normal at the first face, which in the figure is angle 1. The angle of deviation is the angle between the direction of the incident ray (produced) and the emergent ray, which is angle 6.

This is option (D) 1 and 6.

rows.stem: An electric bulb is connected to a power supply of 220 V. If the current drawn by the bulb from the supply is 500 mA, the power of the bulb is :
rows.solution: \(P = VI = 220\ \text{V} \times 0{\cdot}5\ \text{A} = 110\) W (500 mA is 0.5 A). This is option (B) 110 W.

rows.stem: Four identical resistors of \(12\,\Omega\) each are connected in series to form a square ABCD as shown in the figure. The resistance of the network between the two points 1 and 2 is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - where the terminals 1 and 2 attach to the square ABCD (each side a \(12\,\Omega\) resistor) is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
Between points 1 and 2 (the two ends of one side of the square), that side's \(12\,\Omega\) is in parallel with the other three sides in series, \(36\,\Omega\).

\(R = \dfrac{12 \times 36}{12 + 36} = \dfrac{432}{48} = 9\,\Omega\). This is option (C) \(9\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Identify from the following a group containing all non-biodegradable substances.
rows.solution:
DDT, polyester and glass are not broken down by micro-organisms, so all three are non-biodegradable. Leather, cotton, wood, silk and wool are biodegradable.

This is option (C) DDT, Polyester, Glass.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The metals high up in the reactivity series cannot be obtained from their compounds by heating with carbon.

**Reason (R) :** Displacement reactions can also be used to obtain metal.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Metals high in the reactivity series (such as sodium and calcium) hold oxygen more strongly than carbon does, so they cannot be obtained by heating their compounds with carbon. The Assertion is true.

Displacement reactions can indeed be used to obtain metals (as in the thermit process), so the Reason is true, but it does not explain why carbon fails for the very reactive metals.

This is option (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** A mango seed will germinate to form a mango tree.

**Reason (R) :** Heredity determines the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited from parents to offspring.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A mango seed grows into a mango tree and not any other plant, so the Assertion is true.

This is because heredity passes the traits and characteristics reliably from the parent to the offspring, which is the Reason. It is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Nichrome is an alloy which is commonly used in electrical heating devices such as electric irons, toasters, etc.

**Reason (R) :** The resistivity of nichrome is high and its resistance decreases with increase in temperature.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Nichrome is an alloy used in heating devices such as irons and toasters, so the Assertion is true.

Its resistivity is high, but the resistance of nichrome (like that of metals) increases with temperature; it does not decrease, and it does not oxidise readily when hot. So the Reason is false.

This is option (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Animals will not get energy if they eat (consume) coal as food.

**Reason (R) :** Specific enzymes are needed for the breakdown of a particular food.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Animals cannot get energy from coal, so the Assertion is true.

Food is broken down by specific enzymes, each acting on a particular kind of food. Animals have no enzymes that can break down coal, which is why it gives them no energy. The Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
(a) In common practice silver is recovered from silver nitrate solution by the use of copper metal. Name the type of reaction that takes place in this process and give the chemical equation of the reaction involved.

(b) Name the method used for refining silver.
rows.solution:
(a) Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from silver nitrate solution. This is a displacement reaction:

\(\mathrm{2AgNO_3 + Cu \rightarrow 2Ag + Cu(NO_3)_2}\)

(b) Silver is refined by electrolytic refining.

rows.stem:
(a) Select from the following the members of same homologous series :

(1) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CHO}\)

(2) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CO{-}CH_3}\)

(3) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}COOH}\)

(4) \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CHO}\)

(b) What happens to (i) the melting point, and (ii) the solubility of compounds as the molecular mass of the compounds in a homologous series increases ?
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the four compounds in (a) are printed as full structural formulas; the stem carries their condensed formulas, read off the drawings, which name the same compounds. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(a) (1) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\) (propanal) and (4) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CHO}\) (butanal) both have the aldehyde group \(\mathrm{{-}CHO}\) and differ by one \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit, so they belong to the same homologous series. (2) is a ketone and (3) a carboxylic acid.

(b) As the molecular mass increases along a homologous series:

(i) the melting point increases;

(ii) the solubility (in a given solvent) shows a regular gradation, generally decreasing.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: Name the parts of hind-brain of the human brain. Which part of the hind-brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure and salivation ?
rows.solution:
The hind-brain consists of the pons, the medulla and the cerebellum.

Involuntary actions such as blood pressure and salivation are controlled by the medulla.

rows.stem:
Write one function each of the following, in a seed :

(i) Seed coat

(ii) Cotyledon

(iii) Radicle

(iv) Plumule
rows.solution:
(i) Seed coat: protects the seed.

(ii) Cotyledon: stores food for the embryo (the reserve food material).

(iii) Radicle: develops into the root on germination (the future root).

(iv) Plumule: develops into the shoot on germination (the future shoot).

rows.stem: Write the main steps to culture yeast in the laboratory.
rows.solution: To culture yeast: take about 10 g of sugar in a test tube or flask, add about 100 mL of water and dissolve it, then add a pinch of yeast granules. Keep it in a warm place for one to two hours. The yeast grows in the sugar solution and can then be observed under a microscope, showing budding.

rows.stem: Out of the two lenses, one concave and the other convex, state which one will diverge a parallel beam of light falling on it. Draw a ray diagram to show the principal focus of the lens.
rows.solution:
The concave lens diverges a parallel beam of light.

Ray diagram: rays parallel to the principal axis strike the concave lens and spread out after refraction. When the refracted rays are produced backwards (dotted lines), they appear to come from a point F on the principal axis on the same side as the incident light. That point is the principal focus of the concave lens.

rows.stem:
A ray of light after refraction from a convex lens emerges parallel to its principal axis.

(i) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show it.

(ii) In this case, the incident ray before refraction from the lens passes through a point on its principal axis. Name the point.
rows.solution:
(i) Ray diagram: a ray passing through the principal focus \(\mathrm{F_1}\) of a convex lens strikes the lens and, after refraction, emerges parallel to the principal axis on the other side. (Draw the lens with its optical centre O, mark \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and \(\mathrm{F_2}\), and put arrows on the ray.)

(ii) The point is the principal focus (\(\mathrm{F_1}\)) of the lens.

rows.stem: An electric kettle is rated 750 W; 220 V. Can this kettle be used in a circuit which has a fuse of current rating 3 A ? Give reason for your answer.
rows.solution:
Current drawn by the kettle: \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{750}{220} \approx 3{\cdot}4\) A.

No, the kettle cannot be used on that circuit. It draws about 3.4 A, more than the 3 A fuse rating, so the fuse would melt and break the circuit.

rows.stem:
(i) Define the term decomposition reaction. Write one chemical equation each for decomposition reaction where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light or electricity.

(ii) Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is considered an exothermic reaction. Why ?
rows.solution:
(i) A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down to give two or more products.

Energy as heat: \(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

Energy as light: \(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

Energy as electricity: \(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electric current}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(ii) Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost releases heat (energy), so it is an exothermic reaction.

rows.stem: Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions ? Write one chemical equation each for these two types of reactions mentioning the name of the reactant(s) and the product(s) involved in the reactions.
rows.solution:
In a combination reaction two or more substances combine to form a single product, while in a decomposition reaction a single substance breaks down into two or more products. One is the reverse of the other, so they are called opposites.

Combination: \(\mathrm{C(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)}\) + heat. Reactants: carbon and oxygen. Product: carbon dioxide.

Decomposition: \(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\). Reactant: calcium carbonate. Products: calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

rows.stem:
Write the electron-dot structures of (i) sodium, and (ii) oxygen. Using these structures, show the formation of sodium oxide. Mark the anion and cation present in this compound.

(At. No. – Sodium = 11 and Oxygen = 8)
rows.solution:
Electronic configurations: sodium 2, 8, 1 and oxygen 2, 6.

(i) Sodium has one valence electron: drawn as Na with one dot.

(ii) Oxygen has six valence electrons: drawn as O with six dots.

Formation of sodium oxide: each of two sodium atoms transfers its one valence electron to an oxygen atom, which gains two electrons and completes its octet:

\(\mathrm{2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-}\) and \(\mathrm{O + 2e^- \rightarrow O^{2-}}\), giving \(\mathrm{(Na^+)_2O^{2-}}\), that is, \(\mathrm{Na_2O}\).

The cation is the sodium ion, \(\mathrm{Na^+}\), and the anion is the oxide ion, \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\).

rows.stem:
(a) Define hormone.

(b) “Hormones should be secreted in precise quantities. We have a feedback mechanism through which this is done.” With the help of an example justify the statement.
rows.solution:
(a) Hormones are chemical messengers: substances produced in one part of the body that travel to a target organ or tissue and regulate its functions.

(b) The timing and amount of hormone secreted are controlled by feedback. For example, when the blood sugar level rises, cells of the pancreas detect it and secrete more insulin, which lowers the sugar level. As the blood sugar level falls, the insulin secretion is reduced. So the hormone is secreted in just the amount needed.

rows.stem:
The lowest part of the ear called earlobe, is closely attached to the side of the head in some of us (Figure ‘X’), and not in others, called free earlobe (Figure ‘Y’). Attached and free earlobes are two variants found in human populations. The gene for free earlobe is dominant over attached earlobes.

(a) A man with attached earlobes marries a woman having free earlobes. 50% of their children have free earlobes and 50% have attached earlobes. Explain the inheritance of this trait and write the trait combinations of the progeny.

(b) Write the gene combinations of the father and the mother in the above case.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs, Figure ‘X’ (an attached earlobe) and Figure ‘Y’ (a free earlobe); the stem states which figure shows which trait. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) Free earlobe (F) is dominant over attached earlobe (f). The man has attached earlobes, so he must be ff. The woman has free earlobes; since half the children have attached earlobes (ff), each child of that kind received an f from her too, so she must be Ff.

Gametes: woman F and f; man f only.

Children: Ff (free earlobe) and ff (attached earlobe), in the ratio 1 : 1, that is, 50% free and 50% attached.

(b) Father: ff. Mother: Ff.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: A convex lens forms an \(8{\cdot}0\) cm long image of a \(2{\cdot}0\) cm long object which is kept at a distance of \(6{\cdot}0\) cm from the optical centre of the lens. If the object and the image are on the same side of the lens, find (i) the nature of the image, (ii) the position of the image, and (iii) the focal length of the lens.
rows.solution:
(i) The image is on the same side as the object, so it is virtual and erect (and, being 8 cm long, magnified).

(ii) \(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = \dfrac{8{\cdot}0}{2{\cdot}0} = +4\), and \(m = \dfrac{v}{u}\), so \(v = 4u = 4 \times (-6) = -24\) cm. The image is 24 cm from the lens, on the same side as the object.

(iii) \(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-24} - \dfrac{1}{-6} = -\dfrac{1}{24} + \dfrac{4}{24} = \dfrac{3}{24} = \dfrac{1}{8}\), so \(f = 8\) cm.

rows.stem: Three resistors of \(2\,\Omega\), \(3\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\) are connected in (i) series, and (ii) parallel. Draw the arrangements of the resistors and find the equivalent resistance of each arrangement.
rows.solution:
(i) In series (the three resistors one after another): \(R_s = 2 + 3 + 6 = 11\,\Omega\).

(ii) In parallel (the three resistors side by side between the same two points):

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{3 + 2 + 1}{6} = 1\), so \(R_p = 1\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Write the essential function performed by ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere. How is it formed in the upper atmosphere ? Write the name of the group of chemicals mainly responsible for the depletion of ozone layer.
rows.solution:
Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from the sun's ultraviolet radiation, which is highly damaging to organisms (it can cause skin cancer).

It forms when ultraviolet radiation splits some oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms, which then combine with oxygen molecules:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\), then \(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

The chemicals mainly responsible for ozone depletion are the chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

rows.stem:
(i) A compound ‘X’ having two carbon atoms in its molecule turns blue litmus red and 5 – 8% solution of ‘X’ in water is widely used as a preservative. Identify the compound ‘X’ and write its structure.

(ii) Compare its pH nature with a mineral acid.

(iii) ‘X’ on reacting with alcohols produces sweet smelling compounds, used in making perfumes. Name the reaction and write its chemical equation.

(iv) When sodium carbonate is added to ‘X’, a colourless gas is produced which turns lime water milky. Write the chemical equation for the reaction giving the name of the salt produced.
rows.solution:
(i) X is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\): an acid with two carbon atoms, whose 5 to 8% solution in water is vinegar. Structure: \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}C({=}O){-}OH}\).

(ii) Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, so its pH is higher than that of a mineral acid (such as hydrochloric acid) of the same concentration.

(iii) The reaction is esterification:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + H_2O}\)

(iv) \(\mathrm{2CH_3COOH + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + CO_2 + H_2O}\)

The salt formed is sodium ethanoate (sodium acetate); the gas, carbon dioxide, turns lime water milky.

rows.stem:
(i) Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons by giving one example each, with a structural formula.

(ii) Write the method of converting an unsaturated hydrocarbon into a saturated hydrocarbon. Name the industry where this reaction is commonly used.

(iii) Write the name and structure of a hydrocarbon having double bond and four carbon atoms in its one molecule.
rows.solution:
(i) Saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds between their carbon atoms (general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\)). Example: propane, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\).

Unsaturated hydrocarbons have at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms (\(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\) or \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\)). Example: propene, \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_3}\).

(In the answer each structure is drawn with every hydrogen atom shown.)

(ii) An unsaturated hydrocarbon is converted into a saturated one by adding hydrogen in the presence of a nickel or palladium catalyst (hydrogenation):

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni / Pd}} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

It is used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils (making vegetable ghee).

(iii) Butene, \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\): for example but-1-ene, \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\), or but-2-ene, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CH_3}\).

rows.stem:
(i) “The length of the small intestine in various animals depends on the food they eat.” Justify the statement.

(ii) Discuss the role of the pancreas and bile juice in the digestion of food in human beings.

(iii) How is the small intestine designed to absorb digested food ?
rows.solution:
(i) Herbivores eating grass need a longer small intestine to digest the cellulose in it. Meat is easier to digest, so carnivores have a shorter small intestine. So the length depends on the diet.

(ii) The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice, which contains trypsin for digesting proteins and lipase for breaking down emulsified fats.

Bile from the liver makes the food coming from the stomach alkaline so that the pancreatic enzymes can act, and its bile salts break large fat globules into smaller ones (emulsification).

(iii) The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called villi, which increase the surface area for absorption. The villi are richly supplied with blood vessels, which carry the absorbed food to every cell of the body.

rows.stem:
(i) State the role of rings of cartilage present in the throat.

(ii) Discuss the role of the ribs and diaphragm when air is taken in during the breathing cycle.

(iii) Why do we get muscle cramps during heavy exercise ? Explain.
rows.solution:
(i) The rings of cartilage in the throat ensure that the air passage does not collapse when there is little air in it.

(ii) When we breathe in, the ribs are lifted and the diaphragm flattens. This makes the chest cavity larger, and air is sucked into the lungs (alveoli).

(iii) During heavy exercise the muscle cells run short of oxygen and respire anaerobically: pyruvate is converted into lactic acid. The build-up of lactic acid in the muscles causes cramps.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
The given figure shows the current passing through the straight conductor XY.

(i) Copy the diagram and draw the magnetic field lines when current flows from conductor X to Y.

(ii) Name and state the rule used in determining the direction of the magnetic field lines in the situation given above.

(iii) State Fleming’s left hand rule. Using this rule, determine the direction of force applied on an electron entering a uniform magnetic field as shown in the figure.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - two drawings. (i) is to be drawn on a copy of the first: a straight vertical conductor XY passing through a horizontal card Q, in a circuit with a variable resistance, an ammeter A, a battery and a key K. (iii) depends on the second, printed at the top of idx 22: three parallel lines labelled 'Magnetic field' and an electron e with its velocity arrow; the directions of the field and of the electron, which decide the answer, are withheld here. The circuit is on Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
(i) The magnetic field lines around the straight conductor XY are concentric circles centred on the conductor, in the plane of the card Q. With the current flowing from X to Y (downwards through the card), the right-hand thumb rule gives their direction: clockwise when the card is viewed from above.

(ii) The right-hand thumb rule: imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current; then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field lines.

(iii) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

An electron carries negative charge, so the current it represents is opposite to its direction of motion. Applying the rule with the current taken opposite to the electron's velocity, for the field shown in the figure, the force on the electron is out of the plane of the paper (upwards).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
(i) Define the term solenoid. Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines in and around a current carrying straight solenoid. Mark on the pattern the (i) direction of current, (ii) direction of field lines near the ends of the solenoid, and (iii) region where the magnetic field is uniform.

(ii) How would you make an electromagnet using a current carrying solenoid ?
rows.solution:
(i) A solenoid is a coil of many turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

Field pattern: inside the solenoid the field lines are straight and parallel, showing a uniform field; outside they curve round from one end to the other, like the field of a bar magnet. One end acts as a north pole (lines come out) and the other as a south pole (lines go in). The diagram should mark (i) the direction of the current in the turns, (ii) the direction of the field lines near the two ends, and (iii) the region inside where the field is uniform.

(ii) Place a piece of magnetic material such as soft iron inside the current-carrying solenoid. The strong field inside magnetises the soft iron, which then acts as an electromagnet.

rows.stem: Solution P is a strong acid while solution Q is a strong base. On the pH scale, where would you place the solutions P and Q ?
rows.context: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0 – 14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator.
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a plain pH number line marked 0 to 14 and captioned 'pH Scale'; it carries nothing the passage does not state. Page idx 22.
rows.solution: A strong acid has a very low pH and a strong base a very high pH. So P lies near the bottom of the scale (about 0 to 4) and Q near the top (about 12 to 14).

rows.stem: A solution has a pH of 7. Name a compound you would use to (i) increase its pH, and (ii) decrease its pH.
rows.context: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0 – 14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator.
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a plain pH number line marked 0 to 14 and captioned 'pH Scale'; it carries nothing the passage does not state. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
(i) To increase the pH, add a base such as sodium hydroxide.

(ii) To decrease the pH, add an acid such as hydrochloric acid.

rows.stem: When the pH of a solution is decreased from 4 to 2, what effect does it produce on its hydronium ion concentration ? State the colour change shown by the pH paper.
rows.context: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0 – 14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator.
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a plain pH number line marked 0 to 14 and captioned 'pH Scale'; it carries nothing the passage does not state. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
Lowering the pH from 4 to 2 makes the solution more acidic, so the hydronium ion (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) concentration increases (by a factor of about 100).

The colour of the pH paper changes from yellow or orange towards red (pink).

rows.stem: A person is feeling pain and irritation in the stomach due to indigestion. What could be the pH of the fluid in the stomach ? Write the common name of the medicines people use for remedy. Give the chemical name of “milk of magnesia” often used for this purpose.
rows.context: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0 – 14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator.
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a plain pH number line marked 0 to 14 and captioned 'pH Scale'; it carries nothing the passage does not state. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
Indigestion is caused by too much acid in the stomach, so the pH of the stomach fluid is low, about 1 to 3.

People use antacids (mild bases) to neutralise the excess acid. Milk of magnesia is magnesium hydroxide, \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}\).

rows.stem: Write the site of fertilization in human female.
rows.context: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus.
rows.solution: Fertilisation in the human female takes place in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

rows.stem: How does the uterus prepare itself to receive and nurture the growing embryo ? Explain.
rows.context: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus.
rows.solution: Every month the uterus prepares to receive a fertilised egg: its lining becomes thick and spongy and is richly supplied with blood, so that it can nourish the growing embryo.

rows.stem: What happens when the egg is not fertilized ?
rows.context: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus.
rows.solution: If the egg is not fertilised, the thick, spongy lining of the uterus is not needed. It slowly breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus, along with the unfertilised egg. This is menstruation, which occurs roughly every month.

rows.stem: How does the developing embryo get nutrition from the mother’s blood ? Explain.
rows.context: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus.
rows.solution: The embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood through a special tissue called the placenta, which is embedded in the uterine wall. It has villi on the embryo's side, giving a large surface area, and blood spaces from the mother's side around them. Glucose, oxygen and other nutrients pass from the mother's blood to the embryo across it, and the embryo's wastes pass back into the mother's blood.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Name the phenomenon due to which a prism splits the incident white light into a band of colours.
rows.context:
A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure.

A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a triangular prism ABC with a ray labelled 'White light' falling on face AB and a screen S beyond face AC; the passage states all of this. Page idx 26.
rows.solution: The splitting of white light into a band of colours by a prism is called dispersion of light.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: State the reason of getting a band of seven colours in the above case.
rows.context:
A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure.

A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a triangular prism ABC with a ray labelled 'White light' falling on face AB and a screen S beyond face AC; the passage states all of this. Page idx 26.
rows.solution: White light is a mixture of seven colours. A prism bends light of different colours through different angles: violet bends the most and red the least. So the colours separate and form a band (the spectrum).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Explain with the help of a labelled ray diagram, an experimental arrangement to show the recombination of the spectrum of white light.
rows.context:
A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure.

A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a triangular prism ABC with a ray labelled 'White light' falling on face AB and a screen S beyond face AC; the passage states all of this. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
Arrangement: place a second identical prism, inverted with respect to the first, close to it. Let a narrow beam of white light fall on the first prism, which splits it into its colours. The second, inverted prism bends each colour back the opposite way, so the colours recombine and a beam of white light emerges from it, which can be seen on a screen.

This shows that white light is made up of the seven colours.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow.
rows.context:
A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure.

A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a triangular prism ABC with a ray labelled 'White light' falling on face AB and a screen S beyond face AC; the passage states all of this. Page idx 26.
rows.solution: Draw a spherical raindrop with a ray of sunlight entering it. At entry the light is refracted and dispersed into colours; at the back surface of the drop it is reflected internally; where it leaves the drop it is refracted again, and the colours emerge spread apart towards the observer. Arrows must be drawn on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.
